analysis.title: Allocation Views: Investing Through AI Crosscurrents (November 2026)
key_insights: FTIS keeps a 'risk-on' cross-asset stance on robust growth and strong corporate fundamentals, despite October volatility tied to rich valuations for global technology stocks.
AI demand analysis shows consistent adoption despite financing and commoditization concerns. This supports an AI tilt in equity portfolios, overweight the United States, EM ex-China and Japan.

Inflation is the main driver of bond markets. A reflationary US backdrop led FTIS to curtail optimism on US Treasuries and prefer international bonds from weaker-macro countries such as the UK and Canada.
US growth is strong, with the Atlanta Fed GDPNow at 3.7% annualized for the current quarter, driven by consumer spending and capex.
US PCE inflation rose to 3.6% in September and core PCE reached 3.1%, driven by persistent services inflation. Euro area annual inflation rose to 3.8% in September from 3.2% in August.
FTIS believes energy price shocks are not translating into persistent inflation, so longer-term market expectations for rate hikes are broadly overdone.
Global forward earnings are forecast to grow almost 20% over the next 12 months. EM earnings expectations are close to 30%, boosted by semiconductor weighting in EM ex-China indexes.
Forward P/E ratios have fallen below their 10-year median as earnings forecasts outpaced technology price gains in 2026.

AI should not be treated as one trade. Open-weight models with cheaper tokens raise compute demand without raising model providers' revenue, while data-center owners (Google Cloud, Azure, AWS) can raise GPU rental rates.
The upcoming Anthropic IPO is cited as a test case for the view that AI participants are affected differently.
Global AI capex is expected to approach $1 trillion in 2026 and reach $1.7 trillion in 2027. The five largest US hyperscalers are set to spend $800 billion in 2026.
FTIS considers near-term market expectations for US Fed hikes broadly correct, but sees at least three more hikes priced for both the Bank of Canada and Bank of England over 12 months as excessive.
AI companies make up 12% of the US investment-grade bond market. AI borrowing could approach $1 trillion in 2027, and may be crowding out high-yield issuers.
FTIS stays neutral on credit and prefers equity risk. Moving underweight credit is noted as one way to hedge AI exposure if issuance outstrips demand.
US small caps are pressured by higher rates and floating-rate debt. FTIS expects small-cap earnings to fall short of forecasts.
Australian equities are the least-preferred region. The RBA raised its cash rate to 4.85% in early November, a fifth hike this year. Australian bonds were downgraded to neutral.
Japanese government bonds remain underweight but the view improved on momentum. China equities stay neutral because a policy change would lift the market quickly.
Alternatives: energy commodities are seen as a hedge against duration and equity risk given Iran tensions and Strait of Hormuz disruption risk. AI demand should support copper and industrial metals.
Cash is at a maximum underweight, funding overweights in equities, government bonds and alternatives.

sector_views.rationale: Semiconductor earnings are on pace to grow much faster than the S&P 500's more than 15% projected for 2027, and rising memory chip prices lift EM ex-China estimates.
Financial stocks weakened recently, but bank profitability improved with higher rates, boosting EPS growth forecasts.
Energy commodities hedge duration and equity risk amid Middle East tensions, and AI demand supports copper and industrial metals.
Higher rates hit smaller businesses hardest and FTIS expects earnings to fall short of forecasts.

earnings_insights: Global corporate earnings forecast to grow almost 20% over the next 12 months (I/B/E/S estimate, as of Oct 26, 2026). Forecasts have eased slightly.
Next-12-month EPS growth estimates: EM 29.5%, USA 19.4%, ACWI 19.2%, DM ex-US 11.8% (I/B/E/S estimates, Oct 26, 2026).
S&P 500 corporate earnings are projected to grow more than 15% in 2027 (estimate). The semiconductor sector is on pace to grow earnings by much more.
Analysts expect small-cap earnings to grow much faster than large-cap earnings, but FTIS believes they will fall short of forecasts.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Above-trend US growth driven by consumer spending and capex.
Inflation remains well above target, supporting the case for tighter Fed policy.
Persistent services inflation keeps core readings elevated.
Higher energy and services prices. The ECB raised rates in September.
Energy-driven. FTIS sees only one more BoE hike, likely in November.
Fifth hike this year. FTIS thinks more hikes are likely.

macro_indicators.reading: At least three more hikes each over next 12 months
macro_indicators.interpretation: FTIS views this market pricing as excessive given weak growth.

macro_indicators.reading: One more hike in the next six months
macro_indicators.interpretation: FTIS considers this cautious relative to inflation.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight international government bonds (UK gilts, Canada) versus US Treasuries
trade_ideas.rationale: Markets price at least three more hikes from the BoC and BoE, which FTIS considers excessive given anemic growth and weak demand.
trade_ideas.risk: US Treasuries may become a haven if AI credit risk or geopolitical tension rises.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight AI-tilted equities in the US, EM ex-China and Japan
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong earnings growth and forward P/Es below 10-year medians.
trade_ideas.risk: AI capex uncertainty, commoditization and Middle East tensions.

trade_ideas.description: Hold energy commodities within a broad index as a hedge against duration and equity risk
trade_ideas.rationale: Energy price volatility is rising with Iran tensions and Strait of Hormuz risk.
Higher rates hurt floating-rate borrowers and earnings are likely to miss forecasts.
trade_ideas.risk: Small caps can act as a partial hedge against big tech.

risk_factors: AI capex uncertainty and the monetization and commoditization of proprietary AI models.
Rich valuations and concentration in global technology stocks.
Persistent US inflation and a more hawkish Fed.
Middle East tensions and a possible Strait of Hormuz disruption.
AI-related debt issuance crowding out lower-quality issuers and testing Treasury demand when longer-dated issuance rises next year.
Rising US fiscal deficits could expand term premia.
Low European natural gas storage could squeeze margins.
Small-cap floating-rate debt exposure to further rate hikes.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows global PMIs: Services PMI 54.5, Composite PMI Output 54.3, Manufacturing PMI 52.6 (S&P Global, Nov 1, 2026).
Exhibit 2 shows next-12-month EPS growth estimates: EM 29.5%, USA 19.4%, ACWI 19.2%, DM ex-US 11.8% (I/B/E/S, Oct 26, 2026).
Exhibit 4 compares expected 12-month policy rate changes now versus three months ago for the UK, Japan, Canada, Eurozone, US, China and Australia (Bloomberg, Nov 3, 2026).
vol_and_positioning: Equity market volatility in October centered on AI-sensitive themes, which FTIS says has made sentiment and positioning more supportive.
The equity-bond correlation weakened in October as valuation concerns replaced inflation as the main equity driver. Tech stocks fell while government bonds stabilized.
Investment-grade spreads have widened in some sectors from recent lows but still offer a limited cushion. High-yield spread widening is concentrated among lower-quality issuers.
geopolitical: Heightened Middle East tensions are driving a tightening bias in policy expectations in all major regions, including the US.
Tensions in Iran continue and traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is at risk of further disruption, raising energy price volatility.
US tariff threats weigh on Canada.
US midterm elections are expected to have little impact on fiscal policy or bond yields, though budget and debt ceiling debates may cause bond volatility.

tension_points.bull_case: Consistent adoption, ambitious hyperscaler capex ($800B in 2026), almost 20% forward earnings growth and forward P/Es below 10-year medians support equities.
tension_points.bear_case: Open-weight models and cheaper tokens raise compute demand without raising model providers' revenue, hurting FCF. AI debt issuance may crowd out lower-quality issuers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: New issuance meaningfully outstripping demand, which would prompt moving underweight credit to hedge AI exposure.

tension_points.bull_case: Energy shocks weigh on real incomes and demand, so central banks, especially the BoC and BoE, deliver fewer hikes than the three-plus priced.
tension_points.bear_case: Reflationary US backdrop, sticky core inflation and a more hawkish Fed justify US hike expectations and weak Treasury momentum.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of broad-based price acceleration outside energy in Canada, or rising AI credit risk or geopolitical tension that makes US Treasuries a haven.
